productIntent.goal: Provide a lightweight deterministic EVO Runtime Plugin inside a broader composable Enterprise Operating System. EVO itself owns generic BusinessData → supplied PostingRules → Ledger/Balance runtime behavior; platform, application, permission and governance capabilities live outside the plugin.

currentStage.name: Minimal EVO Runtime Plugin Boundary
currentStage.businessGoal: Shrink EVO to the smallest reusable runtime plugin that can accept BusinessData, execute externally supplied rules deterministically, derive Ledger/Balance, and support recalc/clear/export without owning enterprise-platform concerns.

activeRequirementSet.name: Minimal EVO Runtime Plugin Boundary
acceptance: EVO is explicitly defined as a lightweight runtime plugin rather than the enterprise/application platform
identity, users, roles, permissions and authorization policy are outside EVO Core

generic BusinessData submission is the target Core ingestion boundary; Command is optional Host/compatibility orchestration
PostingRule lifecycle/versioning is plugin-owned; Core only executes the supplied rule set

recalculation, runtime-data clear, full export and generic result/status query remain Core runtime-control capabilities
cost, valuation, General Ledger/statutory accounting, financial statements, workflow, SOP, metrics and audit/archive default to plugin ownership

findings: legacy Asloop/bookkeeping semantics include explicit debit/credit concepts
current EVO generic ledger uses signed quantity/amount and does not enforce balanced journals
financial accounting must be layered as an explicit General Ledger projection rather than forcing operational ledgers into debit/credit terminology
invariants: each General Ledger journal has at least one debit and one credit line
sum(debit) equals sum(credit) under pinned accounting precision
financial statements derive from authoritative accounting state and never rewrite canonical BusinessData
